node-1.label: Patient presented with three weeks of jaundice

node-2.label: A 71-year-old man also reported weight loss, abdominal pain, and dark-colored urine over the same three-week period

node-3.label: Patient reported bilateral lower-extremity weakness most noticeable when arising from a chair, resulting in several ground-level falls, with no prolonged periods of being down

node-4.label: Patient had no history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions and takes atorvastatin as a home medication

node-5.label: Physical examination showed significant scleral icterus, epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound, and mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles

why.why: Radiologist, laboratory, and pathology analyses all state that the CT pancreatic head mass with ductal dilatation, markedly elevated CA19-9 (2930), and biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma definitively establish malignant biliary obstruction. The proximal weakness is interpreted as likely paraneoplastic and does not weaken this conclusion. Confidence is raised from 0.98 to 0.99.

Atorvastatin exposure and elevated transaminases/CK initially raised consideration for statin-induced hepatotoxicity, but CT and biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma establish malignant obstruction as the cause of jaundice. Laboratory, pathology, and radiology analyses explicitly exclude statin-induced causes, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.

There is no autoimmune history, and expert analyses confirm pancreatic head adenocarcinoma with malignant biliary obstruction on CT and biopsy. The entire syndrome is explained by malignancy rather than autoimmune hepatitis/myositis, so confidence falls from 0.05 to 0.01.

The patient has obstructive jaundice, but CT shows a pancreatic head mass with ductal dilatation and biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma, directly excluding a benign stone or stricture. All expert analyses explicitly exclude benign biliary obstruction, so confidence is reduced from 0.02 to 0.01.

node-10.label: CT shows a 2.6×3.1 cm pancreatic head mass with pancreatic ductal dilatation

node-11.label: CA19-9 is markedly elevated at 2930 with bilirubin 169.3 and ALP 894

node-15.label: Markedly elevated CK and renal decline are present

node-16.label: Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma causing malignant biliary obstruction

why.why: CT demonstrates a 2.6×3.1 cm pancreatic head mass with pancreatic ductal dilatation; CA19-9 is markedly elevated at 2930; and biliary stricture biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. Laboratory, pathology, and radiology analyses unanimously conclude that these findings definitively establish pancreatic head adenocarcinoma causing malignant biliary obstruction, and the pathologist's biopsy confirmation is the gold standard for tumor diagnosis. Confidence is therefore raised from 0.97 to 0.99.

node-17.label: Proximal lower-extremity weakness is speculated to be a paraneoplastic myopathy associated with pancreatic head adenocarcinoma

attrs.why: The patient has bilateral proximal lower-extremity weakness with elevated CK and no autoimmune/neuromuscular history, in the setting of biopsy-proven pancreatic head adenocarcinoma. Expert analyses interpret the weakness as likely paraneoplastic, although they note it could also be myopathic; because paraneoplastic syndrome is a diagnosis of exclusion and CK elevation can have other causes, confidence is moderate at 0.6.
